name: whisper-medium-sps-persian
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from openai/whisper-medium (config.json max_position_embeddings 1500). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
license: not declared on card (base openai/whisper-medium is Apache-2.0)
notes: ADDED 2026-11-01. Full fine-tune of openai/whisper-medium (24 layers, 1024 hidden, 0.764B) for spontaneous/conversational Persian ASR, 2 epochs, lr 5e-6, 16,409 training segments / 1,985 validation from the SPS corpus. Same tensor set as the base. Recorded because the card prints both rows in one table over the same 500 scored test segments: WER 2.368 -> 0.768 and CER 1.857 -> 0.506, mean segment-level. The size of that gap is the caveat, not just the win: a WER of 2.368 means the stock Whisper-medium is producing roughly 2.4x the reference length of substitutions+deletions+insertions on this material, which is a model failing out of domain rather than a normal baseline, so most of the drop is 'adaptation restored a broken transcript' rather than 'a better ASR'. The corpus is also not distributed with the model, and the numbers are mean segment-level rather than corpus-aggregated, which flatters short segments. Direction is unambiguous; magnitude should not be read as a threefold accuracy gain.

benchmarks.name: WER, Spontaneous Persian Speech (SPS) held-out test, 500 segments
benchmarks.config: Card table '| Model | WER | CER |', mean segment-level error rates over 500 scored test segments: openai/whisper-medium baseline WER 2.368 vs fine-tuned 0.768. Scored as 76.8 (lower is better) rather than 0.768 so it stays on the same 0-100 scale as other WER rows. CER 1.857 -> 0.506 alongside. CAVEAT: mean segment-level, not corpus-aggregated, and the 2.368 baseline suggests heavy degradation of an off-the-shelf model on spontaneous conversational Persian rather than a normal ASR baseline.
